children: Keppel Ltd.'s special dividend from its deal to sell telecommunications unit M1 to StarHub seems to be a mixed bag, says Macquarie Capital's Zhiwei Foo in a note. Most of the deal's consideration is in shares under a 12-month lockup period. He sees a dividend-in-specie of StarHub shares to Keppel shareholders as more likely than an open-market disposal, given the illiquidity of StarHub's shares. He is also less optimistic on the benefits from the Singapore telecommunications market consolidation. Increasing the sector's average revenue per user isn't as straightforward as raising plan prices, given the Singapore government's concern about cost of living, he says. Macquarie downgrades its rating on Keppel to underperform from outperform and slashes its target price to 6.94 Singapore dollars from S$12.87. Shares fall 2.1% to S$8.24. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
